However, music, my dear, is not just about the sheer volume of sound, but also about the interplay and relationship between different voices.

In counterpoint, we strive to create a harmonious blend of voices through careful attention to how each voice moves in relation to the others. By writing all the notes at the same time, you may indeed produce a dense texture, but without the proper care for voice leading and harmonic progression, the result may lack clarity and depth.

Consider a conversation among friends, each taking turns to speak and listen, allowing for a meaningful exchange of ideas. In music, each voice has its own role to play, its own story to tell, and by respecting the rules of counterpoint, we ensure that these voices interact in a coherent and expressive manner.

So, my dear student, while the idea of having all notes sound together may seem appealing, remember that true beauty in music often lies in the subtle dance of voices intertwining and complementing each other. They provide a framework within which composers can express their creativity and communicate their ideas effectively to the listener.

While it is true that composers like Mozart dared to push the boundaries of convention and explore new realms of harmonic language, they did so with a deep understanding of the rules they were breaking. It is through mastery of the traditional techniques that one gains the ability to innovate and transcend them.

So, my dear student, do not fear the rules of music, for they are not shackles but rather stepping stones on the path to artistic growth and expression. Learn them well, respect them, and then, when the time is right, dare to challenge them and carve your own path in the vast landscape of musical creativity.
